text: Mixture of Experts (MoE) is a neural network architecture that routes inputs to different expert subnetworks, allowing for model sparsity and scalability.
In MoE architectures, a gating network determines which experts are activated for each input, improving computational efficiency.
Switch Transformer is a type of MoE model that activates only one expert per token, reducing communication overhead and memory usage.
GShard is a large-scale MoE model developed by Google, enabling training of trillion-parameter models by distributing experts across devices.
MoE models can achieve high performance with fewer active parameters per inference, making them suitable for large language models (LLMs).
A key challenge in MoE is balancing expert utilization to prevent some experts from being overloaded while others are underused.
Recent LLMs like GPT-4 and GLaM have explored MoE architectures to scale up model size without a linear increase in compute cost.
MoE architectures can be combined with traditional transformer layers, where only certain layers use expert routing.
Training MoE models requires careful design of the gating mechanism and loss functions to ensure stable convergence.
Applications of MoE in LLMs include multilingual models, where different experts specialize in different languages or domains.
